reasoningTrail: Shell interpreter /bin/sh spawned by npm (PID 4821) — a package manager has no legitimate reason to execute a shell, strongly indicating supply-chain compromise (T1195.002). Signal: +20.
Sensitive file ~/.aws/credentials was read — AWS credentials contain long-lived access keys that, if exfiltrated, grant full programmatic access to cloud resources (T1552.001). Signal: +35.

Data piped via curl to external IP 198.51.100.4:8443 — this is a non-RFC 1918 address on a non-standard port, consistent with exfiltration to a C2 server (T1048, T1071.001). Signal: +25 (external IP) +20 (pipe to network tool) +10 (non-standard port) = +55.
analysis.remediation:
## Immediate Actions

1. Kill PID 31337 immediately.
2. Block egress to 198.51.100.4 at the host firewall.
3. Rotate AWS credentials — assume they are compromised.

```bash
# Rotate AWS credentials immediately
aws iam delete-access-key --access-key-id <KEY_ID>
aws iam create-access-key --user-name <USERNAME>
# Audit CloudTrail for activity from the leaked key in the last 24h
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=AccessKeyId,AttributeValue=<KEY_ID>
```

4. Audit npm dependencies in `/home/user/project/package.json` for recently updated packages.
5. Snapshot the host for forensic analysis before rebooting.

developerPostmortem.title: CRITICAL: AWS creds exfiltrated via compromised npm dependency (PID 31337)
developerPostmortem.description:
## Summary

At 2026-10-17T07:00:00Z, process PID 31337 — a shell spawned by `npm` (PID 4821) — read `~/.aws/credentials` and transmitted the contents to `198.51.100.4:8443` via `curl`. This is a textbook supply-chain exfiltration pattern (MITRE T1195.002, T1552.001, T1048).

## Impact

AWS credentials are assumed compromised. Any resources accessible with the leaked key must be considered breached until keys are rotated and CloudTrail is audited.
actionItems: Rotate all AWS IAM access keys immediately and audit CloudTrail for the last 24 h.
Identify which npm package introduced the malicious postinstall script — audit `package.json` and lockfile.
Remove or pin the compromised dependency and re-run `npm audit`.
Add `--ignore-scripts` to npm installs in CI pipelines to prevent postinstall execution.
Enable AWS GuardDuty and SCPs to restrict credential use from developer workstations.
